text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Tuesday. Reuters has not veried these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cracks appeared in the civil servants' strike in Mzuzu northern Malawi on Monday which entered its third week as workers disagreed whether to continue or return to work and process their salaries.
- Private hospitals have been caught by a deluge of work as more and more patients flock there for treatment as the appeal to medical staff in government hospitals to return to work goes unheeded.

- The countrywide strike by workers in government seemed to fizzle out at least in Blantyre yesterday when some strikers reported for work normally. But union leader Thomas Banda said although the offices were open and had people in them it did not mean the strike was over.

- Chairman for Commercial Bank of Malawi Khalid Osman has been replaced in a politically motivated move for ignoring instructions that he should not award overdraft applications from leaders of the opposition parties.
